# Vendored librespot crates

Copies of published librespot 0.8.0 crates (MIT licensed, see `LICENSE` in each
directory), wired into the build through `[patch.crates-io]` in
`native/Cargo.toml`. Every local change is marked with a `// SPOTIFYGOOD:`
comment so the patch can be re-applied when upgrading librespot.

| Crate | Why it is vendored |
|-------|--------------------|
| `librespot-core` | Stock `Session::check_catalogue` calls `std::process::exit(1)` for non-Premium accounts, which would kill the Android app. It is patched to report the error and shut the session down instead. |
| `librespot-connect` | The stock crate keeps the Connect state private. The app needs to read the queue and context, edit the queue locally, see the other Connect devices in the account, and implement smart shuffle. |
| `librespot-audio` | The player waits for the data of a stalled stream with a deadline of its own and seeks without waiting for data. The stock API has only `fetch_blocking` for the wait, which requests a failed range again after every failure and starts its timeout anew with every wake-up (it never returned with requests that fail at once), its `Range` isn't public, and its reads always waited for their data. Its loader asked a failing CDN again every round trip by itself, and a read's wait started anew with every failure. It never used the other CDN URLs of a file: the open failed at the first URL that answered with an error status, and the loader stayed on the URL that opened it. |
| `librespot-playback` | Offline playback of downloaded (still encrypted) tracks needs a hook in the track loader; the stock player also calls `exit(1)` on sink errors, gives no way to tell refused audio keys apart, runs one tokio worker per CPU core, measures its position corrections against a 1x line (a stall above 1x was never reported, see Connect item S), and skips a streamed track whose read times out waiting for its data (a stall past the buffer ended the episode); the engine also reads the last packet it decoded (`Player::last_decoded`) to keep a restore point where the audio stopped, and whether a streamed track is all there (`Player::fully_buffered`) to hand it to the offline queue. Its waits for a stream's data are bounded and its seeks don't wait for data (they needed the vendored librespot-audio); its stalls keep the invariants of the "Stalls" section. An MP3 seeks coarsely (`SymphoniaDecoder`): symphonia's accurate MP3 seek continued from the middle of a frame after a read that missed data, so a far load landed seconds late or failed. See `librespot-playback/PATCHES.md`. |

## Patches

`grep -rn SPOTIFYGOOD native/vendor` lists every change. Files that are entirely
new say so in their first line.

### librespot-core

| File | What | Why |
|------|------|-----|
| `src/session.rs` | `check_catalogue` is now a method. For a non-Premium `type` attribute it records `SessionInvalidReason::NonPremiumAccount { account_type }` and calls `Session::shutdown()` instead of `std::process::exit(1)`. It covers the ProductInfo packet and `set_user_attribute(s)`. Adds `pub enum SessionInvalidReason` (`#[non_exhaustive]`) and `pub fn Session::invalid_reason(&self) -> Option<SessionInvalidReason>`. Removes the `process::exit` import. | `exit(1)` would kill the Android app and its foreground service without any UI. |
| `src/config.rs` | `pub const OS: &str = "linux"` (was `std::env::consts::OS`). `os_version()` falls back to `"6.1"` when sysinfo returns nothing or an empty string (was `"0"`). | On `target_os = "android"`, librespot presents the Android-app identity, and Spotify rejects that identity for keymaster-minted credentials. Every platform branch in core matches on this const, so the whole crate now presents the Linux desktop identity: the default client id is keymaster (`SessionConfig::default`, login5), the client-token platform data is `desktop_linux`, the user agent is `Spotify/<desktop version> Linux/0`, the AP handshake uses `PLATFORM_LINUX_*` / `OS_LINUX`, and `spotify_version()` is the desktop one. There are no direct `cfg(target_os)` or `consts::OS` uses in core. Consequence: `Login5Manager::login` (password login) returns `OnlyForMobile`, which the app doesn't use. spotify-player's Termux build applies the same patch. |
| `src/session.rs` (explicit filter) | `Session::set_filter_explicit_forced(bool)` / `filter_explicit_forced()`: an app-side flag (an `AtomicBool` in `SessionInternal`) that `filter_explicit_content()` ORs into the `filter-explicit-content` attribute. | "Hide explicit content" used to be written into that attribute, which is also the account's own (parental) value: ProductInfo replaced it, and an attribute mutation (Spirc flips the local value) or update that met the forced value was taken for the app's own write, so the account's filter could be recorded wrong and later lifted. The attribute now stays the account's value. |
| `src/spclient.rs` | `pub fn RequestOptions::new(metrics: bool, salt: bool, base_url: Option<&'static str>) -> Self`. The fields stay private. | Without it, callers outside the crate can only use the default options with `request_with_options` (metrics and salt on). |
| `src/dealer/mod.rs` | In the reconnect loop, a failing `get_url()` (login5/apresolve) is logged, waits `RECONNECT_INTERVAL` (10 s) and retries, unless the dealer is closed. Before, the `?` ended the dealer for good. The connect-error sleep also aborts on close. | A transient token failure silently killed Connect for the rest of the session. `Dealer::close` no longer waits out the 10 s delay. |
| `src/audio_key.rs` | `AudioKeyError::AesKey { code: u16 }` (was a unit variant), parsed as a big-endian u16 from the `AesKeyError` payload after the sequence number, with no panic on a short payload. Display: `audio key error 0x0001`. Adds `pub const AES_KEY_ERROR_PERMANENT: u16 = 0x0001` and `AES_KEY_ERROR_TRANSIENT: u16 = 0x0002`. Code `0x0001` maps to `ErrorKind::PermissionDenied`, all other codes and `Timeout` map to `ErrorKind::Unavailable` (`Timeout` was `Aborted`). Adds `pub fn is_permanent_denial(err: &Error) -> bool`. The pending sender is removed on timeout and when sending the request fails (it leaked before). Adds a unit test. | Spotify refuses audio keys for some accounts (librespot #1649 / PR #1763). Callers (the vendored playback) need to tell "refused for this account" apart from throttling. |
| `src/dealer/protocol/request.rs` | **Unchanged.** serde ignores unknown fields (there is no `deny_unknown_fields` anywhere), so a `set_options` with extra fields such as `modes` still parses. A connect test covers this. Note that a present `options` object needs all three `OptionsOptions` bools. | Checked, no change needed. |
| `src/cache.rs` | `Cache::save_file_of_len(file, contents, len)` (and `save_file` through it): the file is written next to its place (`<name>.part<pid>-<n>`), checked against `len` when given, synced, and renamed to its place; a failed save removes its partial file and returns its error (it was `CacheError::Path`); the size limiter counts the file once it is in place. Opening the cache removes the partial files another process left. | A save that failed partway (no space left for the second copy, the process ended) left what it had written under the final name: it loaded as the complete file (`Cache::file`), and the track ended at the cut on every play until the file was evicted. A concurrent open could see a half written file. The tests are in librespot-audio (this crate can't run its own: dev-dependencies outside the workspace). |

### librespot-audio

The crates.io package `librespot-audio 0.8.0`, unchanged except for the hunks below
(`Cargo.lock`, `Cargo.toml.orig` and `.cargo_vcs_info.json` removed, `LICENSE` (MIT) copied).

| File | What | Why |
|------|------|-----|
| `src/fetch/mod.rs` | `StreamLoaderController::read_position()` (where the file is read, `None` if it isn't streamed), `fetch_range(start, length)` (requests the bytes once, within the file) and `range_available_at(start, length)`. | The vendored player's bounded wait for the data of a stalled stream (one request, a deadline from its start); `fetch_blocking` didn't return with requests that fail at once and drained the per-domain rate limit, and `Range` isn't public. |
| `src/fetch/mod.rs` (seeks, reads) | `StreamLoaderController::set_fail_fast(on)`: while on, a read of data that isn't there fails at once (`TimedOut`) and requests nothing; `missed()` is the first offset such a read missed. `is_loader_gone()`: the loader ended (its command channel is closed). `AudioFileStreaming::read` waits for its data until one deadline from its start (`download_timeout`), and a loader that is gone fails it (`BrokenPipe`) only when its data isn't there. `open` is split (`open_urls`, after the CDN URL resolve). `stalled_for_tests(file_size, downloaded)` and `partial_for_tests(file_size, downloaded range, read_position)` (`#[doc(hidden)]`): a streamed file's controller whose rest never comes, for the vendored player's tests. | The vendored player seeks without waiting for data (PATCHES.md "Stalls" (b)): symphonia's Ogg seek bisects the whole file and each probe past the data waited `download_timeout` on the player thread. Every notify (also of a range that failed) started a read's timeout anew, so failing requests kept it, and the player thread, from returning. Stock failed a read of data that was there when only its read-ahead couldn't be requested. The tests open a local server. |
| `src/fetch/mod.rs` (temp files, cache) | A stream's temp file is made by `temp_buffer`, which makes the session's `tmp_dir` again when it is missing; when no temp file can be made at all, the stream is kept in memory (`MemoryFile`, `StreamOutput`, `StreamInput`; such a stream isn't saved to the cache) instead of failing its load. The cache save of a complete stream goes through `Cache::save_file_of_len` with the temp file's length (see librespot-core). | The engine keeps `tmp_dir` in the app's cache dir, which Settings' "Clear cache" or a system cache trim empties while the session lives: every open failed (NotFound) after the CDN's answer, every load was Unavailable (a network error) until a new session. A save that failed partway left a cut file that played as complete. |
| `src/fetch/mod.rs` (CDN URLs) | `open_urls` tries every URL until one answers with the file's first bytes: an error status, or a `Content-Range` it can't read (`content_range`, checked splits; stock sliced it at indexes that a malformed header made panic), goes on to the next one, like a transport error. When all fail, the last status is returned (`Unavailable` when none answered). `AudioFileShared::cdn_urls` keeps all of them for the loader, with the ones that answered that they can't deliver marked dead. URLs are logged by their index (they carry a token). | Stock failed the open at the first URL that answered at all: while the first CDN of storage-resolve's list failed (a 5xx, or a 403/404 for the region), every load failed (`NetworkError`, Spirc skipped on), and a reopen started with the same URL again. |
| `src/fetch/receive.rs` | `ResponseTime` is sent only for a response with data (206): it was sent before the status check. A failed request sends `ReceivedData::Failed(status)`: the loader's prefetch stays off until data comes again, and every request (a reader's `Fetch` too) waits out a backoff (500 ms, doubling to 8 s, reset by data); the ranges asked for meanwhile are requested when it ends. An expired or invalid URL (401, 403, 404, 410), or one that failed `URL_FAILURES_MAX` (3) times in a row, is left for the next URL of the file that isn't dead (in turn, `AudioFileFetch::url`), which is asked at once for what failed and for what waited for the backoff (`ReceivedData::Failed { status, url, missing }`; a failure of a URL it has left asks the current one); once no URL is left the loader ends. A request that gets no response, or no part of its body, for `download_timeout` fails (a transport error, the backoff); the body is read frame by frame, and what came before a failure is kept. | The loader never loops on errors (PATCHES.md "Stalls" (e)): the `ResponseTime` of a failed response woke its loop, and the prefetch asked for the same range again, every round trip, playing, stalled or paused, until it drained the per-domain rate limit (which ended it) or the track was unloaded. An ended loader lets the player open the file again with new URLs at once. It stayed on the URL that opened the file: a CDN that failed kept the track stalled until it paused, while the other CDNs worked. Requests had no timeout: on a network that silently drops its packets (a Wi-Fi without internet after Android switched to LTE) one hung for good and held the file's only download slot, so the track stalled until it paused. |
| `src/fetch/mod.rs`, `src/fetch/receive.rs` (tests) | A CDN on localhost that fails as asked: a failing CDN is asked once per request (no loop, the loader survives 5xx), an expired URL ends the loader (a read fails at once, the data that is there still plays), a read waits once, a fail-fast read misses at once without a request, a request that gets no answer gives up and frees the download slot. A stream whose `tmp_dir` is gone makes it again, one whose `tmp_dir` can't be made keeps its bytes in memory (the bytes read are the CDN's), a memory file's own positions; a cache save that fails partway leaves no file (nor one shorter than its length), a complete one is there, and partial files another process left are removed when the cache opens. With two CDNs: the open goes on to the next one (after a 503, a 403, a 404, a refused connection) and fails with the last status when both fail; a loader goes on with the other one when its URL expires (at once, for the range that failed) and ends when none is left (a dead one isn't asked again), and leaves one that fails 3 times in a row. The backoff and the dead statuses. (`cargo test -p librespot-audio`; the crate can't have dev-dependencies, the tests use the tokio features librespot-core enables.) | |

### librespot-connect

| File | What | Why |
|------|------|-----|
| `Cargo.toml` | tokio features `rt` and `time` are now listed. | `tokio::spawn` (suggestion fetches), `sleep` and `timeout`. Before, these only worked through feature unification with core. |
| `src/snapshot.rs` (new), `src/lib.rs` | Public read-only types `ConnectSnapshot` (with `ending`, see A), `SnapshotTrack`, `TrackProvider`, `SnapshotPlayStatus` and `SpircCommandError`. | The app needs the state, which upstream keeps private. |
| `src/state/snapshot.rs` (new) | `ConnectState::snapshot()` builds the snapshot. `can_skip_prev` is true whenever a track is current: without a previous track, previous restarts it, so the restriction reason "no previous tracks" alone doesn't disable it (it did on the first track of a load and after every shuffle). `snapshot_fingerprint()` is a cheap hash, so Spirc skips the rebuild when nothing visible changed. The position is hashed as its nominal start while playing, so re-anchoring on each PUT doesn't count as a change; at another speed it is the start of the line of the playing speed, rounded to 50 ms, and the snapshot reports the playing speed while playing (Spirc item S). | Snapshot stream (A). |
| `src/spirc.rs` | **A** `subscribe_state()`. A `watch` channel, published with `send_if_modified` at the bottom of every loop iteration and once in `Spirc::new`. The final snapshot, sent after the epilogue, has `ending: true` and is the state when the loop ended, before the epilogue's disconnect (a task that ended by itself would otherwise report "stopped, inactive" and hide what was playing). `is_running()` tells whether the task still takes commands: the channel is closed as soon as the loop ends (it stayed open for the whole epilogue), and a `Shutdown` left in it is still honoured (the player is paused). **B** `add_to_queue`, `remove_from_queue`, `move_queue_item`, `clear_queue`, `skip_to` (active only). `add_to_queue` fails right away (FailedPrecondition, `StateError::QueueFull`) when the queued tracks plus the adds not handled yet fill the 80 next tracks (a shared gauge, kept by the task); the task checks again, and the remote `add_to_queue` endpoint now fails instead of dropping the track. After every queue change, local or remote (`add_to_queue`/`set_queue`), and after shuffle changes, the next track is preloaded again if a preload had already been triggered. **C** `subscribe_cluster()` publishes `Option<Arc<Cluster>>` from the NEW_DEVICE PUT, from every cluster push, and from state/volume/audio-output PUT responses that parse as a cluster with devices. `refresh_cluster()` (allowed while inactive) puts the state to get a fresh cluster; a failure is only logged. **D** `smart_shuffle(bool)`. Suggestions are fetched off the loop (`tokio::spawn` + `get_autoplay_context` with about 20 sampled context track uris, bounded by 20 s), at most one request at a time, and delivered back through a new `select!` arm. The request is aborted when its result becomes invalid and when the task ends (also when its future is dropped), so it never keeps the session alive. Results are dropped if the generation or context changed. Pacing: 30 s minimum between fetches, 5 min after an empty result, 30 s doubling to 10 min on errors, at most 40 pending suggestions. Suggestions are refetched after a load, a reshuffle, or a change to the default context through the resolver. **E** `set_audio_output(kind, name)`, allowed while inactive, PUTs with `AUDIO_DRIVER_INFO_CHANGED` only when the value changed. **F** Shutdown sets the flags first and never fails. The disconnect and the epilogue's DELETE and dealer close are each bounded by 3 s. A closed command channel (all handles dropped) is treated as shutdown, and a closed player event channel stops being polled (both were busy loops). No handler awaits a state put any more (`StatePuts`): every command, the remote transfer, the activation, `refresh_cluster`, `set_audio_output` (AUDIO_DRIVER_INFO_CHANGED), the volume puts, the put after a resolve and the delayed background put only request one. At most one put is in flight, bounded by 5 s and polled by the loop next to the commands and player events; the ones requested meanwhile wait, at most one of each kind, and are built when sent (so they carry the state of then). The handlers used to await their put without a bound (spclient retries and sleeps out a 429's Retry-After), so a pause (headphones unplugged, a call) or the end of a track waited behind the put of the previous command, for up to a minute. A put failure is logged, not reported as the command's failure (the command was applied). A put that times out or fails transiently is sent again after 2 s and then 10 s (with the state of then), unless a newer put of its kind supersedes it, then it is given up; it used to be dropped, so Spotify and the other devices kept the old state (e.g. still playing after a pause) until some later put. A disconnect, an inactive state and a connection id update (NEW_DEVICE) drop the puts in flight or waiting first, so that none lands after them. The two requests of `handle_disconnect` stay awaited, each bounded by 5 s (the local state becomes inactive either way); the transfer request of an inactive device is bounded by 10 s; every context fetch is bounded by 10 s (`ContextResolver::get_next_context`, a load awaits the first one). The NEW_DEVICE put that announces the device (its response is the first cluster) is bounded by 30 s; the task then ends like after a failed dealer setup (a live task never delivered its first cluster). That is only the first connection (the commands wait until it is established): after a reconnect of the dealer the announce is a put of StatePuts (`StatePut::NewDevice`: 5 s, sent again after a failure, the puts requested meanwhile wait behind it), and the loop goes on. It was awaited for up to 30 s with no command, player event or cluster handled (a pause from unplugged headphones, the end of a track), and a failure ended the task, paused the playback and built the session again. `Drop for SpircTask` pauses the player unless spirc stopped it: a task that ended by itself, or was aborted in the middle of a handler (so `handle_shutdown` never ran), left it playing. Commands are now always polled: anything other than `Shutdown` that arrives before the connection is established is buffered, so an early shutdown no longer hangs. That includes the dealer start before the loop: it is raced against `Shutdown` (which ends the task right away) and bounded by 30 s (the task then ends, like after a failed start). **G** `ConnectConfig.auto_takeover` gates the startup takeover. The takeover restores playback paused (`handle_transfer(.., start_paused)`). **I** `last_error` in the snapshot, plus `subscribe_errors()` (`broadcast`, capacity 16). Commands that are ignored while inactive now report `NotActive` (FailedPrecondition). **J** Cluster update without a cluster while active also stops the player, and so does the transfer-away branch (another device became active); both stop it before their requests (it played on until they gave up), publish the snapshot as inactive and stopped before the (bounded) requests, so that commands follow the device that took over instead of queueing behind the requests and being dropped as not active, and forget the request id. `handle_disconnect` becomes inactive even if the state update fails (it returned early, so the device kept reporting itself as active). `prev` with repeat and no prev tracks loads the track; without repeat it restarts the current track (it stopped playback). FilterExplicitContentChanged is emitted for both values. A remote `skip_next` to a uri that isn't in the next tracks falls back to a plain next, where before it consumed the queue, stopped playback, or never ended. **K** `set_autoplay(bool)` sets the local `autoplay` user attribute. It fails when `SessionConfig.autoplay` overrides it. Once set, the local value wins: `attributes:mutated` for autoplay is ignored (it used to flip the local value, which no longer mirrors the account), `attributes:update` keeps it, and Spirc reads the local value even if the attributes are replaced. Enabling queues an autoplay resolve; disabling drops pending autoplay resolves and the autoplay context unless autoplay is already playing. **M** An inactive spirc ignores all player events: the app's offline playback drives the same player, and an inactive spirc used to adopt those request ids and stop the player at the end of every offline track. `release_player()` hands the player back to the app once it detached the spirc: the task stops handling events (it shuts down at once) and never drives the player again (no load, play, pause, seek, preload or stop, also not from a handler that was waiting on a request, its shutdown or `Drop`): the app's offline playback may already run on it, and the app pauses what the detached spirc played. A load from a uri asks the resolver again even if the same context failed a moment ago, and only a context that can't be resolved (not found, not allowed, invalid) is skipped for a while; a transient failure (network, rate limit, server error) used to refuse that context without any request for 60 s. **L** `PlayerEvent::Unavailable` uses the reason: transient failures (`KeyTemporarilyDenied`, `NetworkError`) don't mark the track unavailable for the session (it is skipped, not blacklisted), and a failed preload only preloads the following track for track-specific reasons. A track refused (`NotAvailable`) while the explicit filter is on is noted (`ConnectState::note_filtered_unavailable`); once the effective filter is off (the player's `FilterExplicitContentChanged`, handled also while inactive, with the session's value), those marks are forgotten (`forget_filtered_unavailable`): the context tracks get their provider back and the next tracks are rebuilt from the playing track. They stayed unavailable for the whole Spirc session: skipped by every fill up and every context resolved later, hidden from Up Next and the other clients, never suggested. After a key denial or a transient failure the chain of preloads walked the whole queue with one key request per track while a track played; that track is now loaded, and its failure handled, when the current one ends. **N** Play and play/pause while stopped but active (the context ended, or the player was halted after refused loads) play the current track again from its start, like the remote resume; without a current track they fail (`NothingToPlay`, FailedPrecondition). They were ignored and reported success (`play_action`). **Q** A load fetches its context before it tears down the playing one (`prefetch_load_context`, bounded like every fetch): a failed or timed out fetch fails the load with its own error (DeadlineExceeded, NotFound, ...) and leaves the playback, Up Next, shuffle and repeat as they were. It used to fail only after all of them were gone, with NoContext, and the playback stopped after the song. A start track that isn't in the context yet: a start uri plays itself, outside the context, followed by the pages that are there, and is placed in the context as soon as its page is there (`place_current_track_when_resolved`, dropped once another track plays; it plays before the context if it isn't on any page). A shuffled load shuffles the pages that are there right away, the last page shuffles the whole context again. Both used to leave the next tracks empty until the last page, so the playback stopped when the song ended meanwhile (a restore or resume of an artist session on a flaky link); a start uid (no track to play) resolves the further pages right away until it is found (20 s at most). Either fell back to the first track at the position of the requested one (a restore or resume of an artist session). **R** A received transfer is finished with the first resolve of its context (`ContextResolver::finish_transfer_early`): the transferred queue and the next tracks of the pages there are, and a transferred track that isn't on them yet is placed once its page is there (as for a load, see Q; not while shuffled, the last page's shuffle puts it first: the placement replaced the shuffled next tracks with the album order after it). It waited for the last page with empty next tracks, so the song ending, or a Next, meanwhile stopped the playback. After a further page of the default context the next track is preloaded again (a preload triggered while the next tracks were empty) and the state is put. **P** A resolve of the loop that fails is retried, and the state is still set up when it fails for good (see `src/context_resolver.rs`); the resolve a load waits for isn't retried, the load reports the failure. A given up resolve of the default context marks it incomplete, so a load of it resolves it again; a load skips the resolve only for a context that is resolved and all there. **O** A load that resets the context completely (another uri, or a track list) drops the resolves and the transfer still pending for the previous context (`reset_context` tells it). Only a load of another uri did: after a track list load, the album pages of an artist played a moment before were appended to the new list, and they deferred its shuffle. **S** `set_playback_speed(speed)`, allowed while inactive: the speed the app's sink plays at (podcasts). The state's `playback_speed` while playing is that speed (was always 1), so other clients extrapolate the position at the real rate; the position reached at the previous speed is the new anchor, and an active device puts the state once. The stock player measured its position corrections against a 1x line: below 1x it reported one every second or two, above 1x none, also after a stall (a blocking read of a streamed file) or a slow seek, so the position ran ahead of the audio by speed x stall. The vendored player now gets the speed (`Player::set_playback_speed`, from spotcore's `player.setSpeed`) and keeps its line at that speed (see `librespot-playback/PATCHES.md`): a correction comes after a stall, and after every seek (its first packet). While playing at another speed, a position (a correction, or the Playing event of a resume) within 500 ms of the position at the playing speed (`ConnectState::on_playing_line`) only keeps Spirc's own (1x) anchor current, with no state put; any other one re-anchors the state (the 100 ms check on Spirc's 1x lines is skipped then: a stall at 2x can come out on the same 1x line). Every position follows the speed. The re-anchor before each put (`update_position_in_relation`, through `ConnectState::prepare_put` for `send_state_put` and `notify`) advances at the state's speed; it added the time at 1x, so above 1x every put (a volume key, the device sheet's refresh, a queue add) moved the position back by (speed - 1) x the time since the anchor, sent it to Spotify and the other clients, and nothing corrected it. A paused position no longer advances at a disconnect either. Spirc's own position (`handle_pause`, `handle_prev`, a speed change) is the anchor advanced at the playing speed (`ConnectState::playing_position`); the 1x nominal start time drifted from it. A speed change re-anchors the nominal start time too. While playing, the snapshot reports the playing speed: the state's own is only brought up to date with the next put, so right after a resume the snapshot said 1. Its fingerprint hashes the line of that speed (its start to 50 ms, exact at 1x), so the re-anchors don't republish it. An incoming transfer advances the transferred position at its `playback_speed`. **T** A shuffled load with `Options.shuffle_order` (a reconnect restore, the offline queue's hand-back) keeps that order instead of a new shuffle (`ConnectState::shuffle_in_order`): the context tracks matching the given ids (by uid, else by uri; ids no longer in the context are left out) in their order, then the rest of the context, shuffled with a new seed. The start track plays at its place in it, with the given tracks before it as the prev tracks (up to 10); after a start track that isn't one of them (or one outside the context) the given ones come next. Without a match it shuffles as before. While further pages resolve, each one is placed in the order as it comes (`place_in_order`): its given tracks go to their places, its other tracks are shuffled in after the playback position, the playback goes on where it is, and a start track that played outside the context goes to its place once its page is there (it isn't placed in the album order, as with R). The last page (`try_finish`), or a failed one (`finish_after_failure`), keeps the order instead of shuffling the whole context again. Every reconnect drew a new order: Previous restarted the song, Up Next changed and the songs already heard came back. **U** Whether the next track plays (Next, also on EndOfTrack and Unavailable, Prev and skip_to) comes from Spirc's own status (`continues_playing`), and the state's play flags (with their restrictions) follow the status at the end of every loop iteration while active. Both came from the flags of the last put built: a put waiting behind one in flight (StatePuts) left them at the status before a pause or resume for up to its timeout, so Next after a pause played the next song out loud and Next after a resume loaded it paused. The announce after a dealer reconnect (NEW_DEVICE, which drops the waiting put) is prepared like a put (`prepare_put`): it carried the status and position of the last put built, and nothing put the state again. **V** A stalled stream (the vendored player's `PlayerEvent::Stalled`) re-anchors the state at the position played and shows LoadingPlay (buffering, no extrapolation) until the PositionCorrection of its first packet after the data came, which goes on as Playing. It stayed Playing, so the seek bar, a -15 s from there (the app's base is the extrapolated position), the progress saved and the other clients ran ahead by speed x stall. Nothing moves it meanwhile: the state's `playback_speed` is the speed only while Playing (0 while loading or stalled, so the other clients don't extrapolate either), and the re-anchor before a put (`prepare_put`, also of a retry, and `handle_disconnect`) moves only Playing; every put of a stall, and its retries on the dead network, moved the position on by speed x the time since the anchor. A Loading event Spirc didn't ask for (the player opens its track again by itself after a stall or with a loader that is gone, see the vendored player's `reopen`) goes LoadingPlay from Playing and LoadingPause from Paused, at the event's position (`loading_status`); right after Spirc's play it went Playing from 0:00 (the seek bar, the snapshot the app saves the episode's resume point from, and the other clients), and a reopen that failed skipped the episode (the player now pauses at its position instead). The engine's network-loss deferral counts a Playing snapshot only: a stall plays nothing to cut off, and the restore point it freezes is capped at the last packet heard (also for LoadingPlay). **W** A transfer received while the other device plays autoplay (an album ended, autoplay went on; a librespot device marks its autoplay tracks, Spotify's are marked the same way) is finished: the transferred track is an autoplay track, so `handle_transfer` resolves the autoplay context (while autoplay is on) and the state is set up once it is there; without it (its resolve failed, autoplay is off) the transfer is finished after the end of the default context, so the finished album doesn't start over. The transferred queue comes first either way. The state was switched to an autoplay context nothing resolved (handle_transfer went by the provider, which a transferred track never had), `finish_transfer` failed, the transferred queue was dropped, Up Next stayed empty, and shuffle and repeat stayed disallowed. A shuffled transfer (the device shuffled the context and kept the option on when autoplay took over) goes on in autoplay as well, the shuffle option kept: the shuffle made the default context the active one again and played the finished one anew, reshuffled, before autoplay came back, and an autoplay context that didn't allow shuffling failed the transfer (round 20). **X** A received transfer always finishes: its resolve is queued also when the same context failed for good within the last minute (`ContextResolver::add_requested`, like a load); `add` dropped it, and the transfer waited for good (Up Next empty, the transferred queue lost, the playback stopped after the current song), e.g. a second transfer of the same session within a minute. A plain track list (`spotify:web-api`, this app's or a librespot device's, which can't be resolved) is made of the tracks the transfer brought, like a session without a context uri (its resolve could only fail), and starts over (a list played here before has the same uri). A transfer that doesn't wait for a resolve is finished like a resolved one (`finish_transfer`: the transferred queue was dropped, and a current track the tracks didn't contain failed the transfer), and one whose awaited resolve isn't queued is finished at once with what it brought (`finish_transfer_without_resolve`). | See the items in `connect.md` §15. |

New state: `skipped_uids`, `smart_shuffle`, `suggestions`, `used_suggestion_uris`. `set_audio_output()`. `put_state_request(reason)` (a copy of the request for Spirc's state puts; `notify_volume_changed` is gone). `StateError::CanNotFindTrackInQueue`. `reset_playback_to_position` keeps a track that isn't part of the context (queued, a playing suggestion, or removed by a context update) as the current track. | `src/state/smart_shuffle.rs` (new) | Local smart shuffle. Suggestions are keyed by the pass through the default context (`index.page`, the wraps with repeat) and the position in the shuffled default context after which they are inserted (one after every 3rd context track, continuing into the following passes with repeat, up to the end of the context without), so each one is inserted once and are never added to `StateContext.tracks`, so unshuffle keeps working. They keep the `context` provider, carry the metadata `smart_shuffle.suggested=true`, and take the `context_index` of the track they follow. Already-suggested uris and uris of the context are filtered out. Without repeat, suggestions for later passes are dropped (a stale one blocked every new batch). | D |

Autoplay tracks that are already there are skipped. Before a further page of the playing default context is appended, the next tracks past the end of the context so far are dropped (the wraps of repeat, or the transition to autoplay; the fill up rewinds to the end in the same pass), so the new tracks come next: the 10 top tracks of an artist wrapped about 7 times before its albums played. `update_context` appends its own further pages without that (`append_page`). Notes for users of the connect patches:
- Snapshot clock: `position_timestamp_ms` is local epoch milliseconds (the same clock as `System.currentTimeMillis()`). The position now is `position_ms + (now - position_timestamp_ms) * playback_speed`, and `playback_speed` is 0 unless the status is `Playing`. Internally, Spirc puts server-corrected timestamps (`local + time_delta`).
- `next_tracks` and `prev_tracks` include hidden delimiters (`hidden == true`, uri `spotify:delimiter`). Filter them out for display.
- Only `subscribe_*`, `is_running`, `set_audio_output`, `set_autoplay`, `refresh_cluster`, `activate`, `transfer` and `shutdown` work while the device is inactive. Every other command reports a `NotActive` error. To control another device, use spclient directly.
- Smart shuffle is local. Other clients see the suggestions as ordinary context tracks, and the mode is not sent to Spotify (`modes` is not set).
